name: fit-in-the-holes
why: check_fit on the worker the corpus shares, which no case called before this one. A worker keeps what it built between requests, keyed by what each subtree is, and from fdd010e7 (2026-09-14) it read a reference's keys by node position in the part: the block, whose node 0 is itself, came back as the plate, the part's node 0, interfering by the plate's whole volume; each pin, whose node 1 is its move, came back as the 20 mm cutter at the origin, the part's node 1. A reference that missed was kept under the part's keys, and the next evaluation of any part with that cutter at the origin built the reference in its place (docs/GOTCHAS.md). Closed forms: the block is 0.25 mm clear of the square hole's walls and spans +-9.75 x +-9.75 x +-15; the 9.5 mm pin is 0.25 mm clear of the 10 mm bore all round and spans 15.25..24.75 by +-4.75; the 10.5 mm pin shares the ring pi (5.25^2 - 5^2) x 10 = 80.503 mm3. Bounds are read off each solid's mesh, so a round side can sit up to the 0.01 mm deflection inside its radius. The plate is 60 x 40 x 10 less the square hole and the bore, 24000 - 4000 - 250 pi = 19214.602 mm3; its mesh reads 0.005 % over, the bore's chords. Every fit is asked twice after the part's evaluation, so the second answer is built from the worker's cache and must match the first.
